doubt_decisions.doubt: telefoon: the new sentence repeats the general 'Wij bellen u als de telefoon klaar is.'
doubt_decisions.decision: Keep. The repetition tells a Saturday customer that the slower repairs get no fixed day, unlike the screen's Monday. Naming a weekday would mean counting 2 or 3 days across the closed Sunday, which a learner could contest. The paragraph follows the spec's suggested fix, and 'Bij een oplaadaansluiting' is clipped but in the folder's register and maps onto the table row.

doubt_decisions.doubt: terugbrengen q1: add 'niet gewassen' so every condition is entailed literally?
doubt_decisions.decision: Do not add. The price tag is a condition a reader cannot infer, so it had to be stated; an unworn jacket has not been washed. No option turns on washing (option C's 'niet meer' is the 30-day limit), and adding it would stretch the prompt to 38 words.

doubt_decisions.doubt: terugbrengen q2: key C is now the longest option by characters (49 against 44 and 41).
doubt_decisions.decision: Keep. All three options have eight words in the same 'Ja/Nee, want …' frame, and the checker's per-text threshold is not reached. Batch-wide the key is the longest option in 4 of 20 questions, below chance, so length gives no strategy. The prescribed option A copies the rule sentence and is a strong lure; padding B or rewording the key would change fields outside the fix list for no gain to the learner. The 021 review's 'no key longest by words or characters' no longer holds by characters for this one question; I accept that.

doubt_decisions.doubt: ramen q2: key A was already the longest option by characters.
doubt_decisions.decision: Keep (predates the fix, outside the fix list). A ties with D at eight words, and the fix only shortened C by one character.

doubt_decisions.doubt: politiebureau q2: 'Waar moet zij kijken?' instead of the spec's example 'Waar kan zij kijken?'.
doubt_decisions.decision: Keep 'moet'. It mirrors the instruction 'Kijk op …', fits all three options as places to look, and asks what the text tells her to do, so option A (going to the police station anyway) cannot be argued the way it could be under 'kan'.

doubt_decisions.doubt: Checker 'longest sentence' warnings for telefoon (48) and gezinskaart (45).
doubt_decisions.decision: Accept. These are artefacts of the splitter reading header and table lines as one sentence; the longest real sentences are 13 and 17 words.

items.level_reason: Repair folder with a four-row table, 166 words, prose average 7.0 and longest sentence 13. q1 combines the 12.00 cut-off with a one-day step and q2 applies the Saturday exception: two details per question, typical of the exam. The fix adds one rule sentence and does not change the level (004–005 level check: comparable).
items.fix_verified: 'U kunt de telefoon dan op maandag ophalen.' (every repair on Monday, which contradicted 'in 2 dagen' and 'in 3 dagen') is replaced by 'Een nieuw scherm is dan op maandag klaar. Bij een oplaadaansluiting of waterschade bellen wij u als de telefoon klaar is.' A Saturday screen is now ready on Monday, the next opening day after the closed Sunday, which is consistent with 'de volgende dag'; the 2- and 3-day repairs get no fixed day. The q2 evidence and explanation follow the new text.

evidence.quote: Brengt u hem later? Dan is het scherm de volgende dag klaar.

distractors.A: Dinsdag needs a drop-off before 12.00 ('Brengt u de telefoon vóór 12.00 uur? Dan is een nieuw scherm dezelfde dag klaar.'); 14.00 is later.
distractors.C: Donderdag is 'in 2 dagen', the oplaadaansluiting row of the table, not the screen.
distractors.D: Zaterdag borrows the Saturday paragraph; Julio comes on Tuesday.

evidence.quote: Op zaterdag doen wij alleen batterijen. Andere reparaties nemen wij op zaterdag wel aan. Een nieuw scherm is dan op maandag klaar. Bij een oplaadaansluiting of waterschade bellen wij u als de telefoon klaar is.

distractors.B: Tempting through the table's 'dezelfde dag' and the before-12.00 rule, but on Saturday 'Een nieuw scherm is dan op maandag klaar.'
distractors.C: Accepted on Saturday but not repaired that day ('alleen batterijen'); the table gives 2 days and the shop calls when it is ready.

evidence.quote: U betaalt bij het ophalen.

distractors.B: The call only says the phone is ready ('Wij bellen u als de telefoon klaar is.').
